beats.text: Out, all of you. Road ends here. Camp is half a kilometre on foot.

beats.text: So the road's finished. You felt it go soft?

beats.text: That's what I told you. And that shoulder. That shoulder's no good.

beats.text: Ilvar's last unclimbed face. Six expeditions tried it and took the hint.

beats.text: That's it? The one in the photograph?

beats.text: That's it. Cloud's wrong today. Should be blowing east. It's leaning south.

beats.text: How can you possibly know that?

beats.text: Pressure changed an hour ago. I felt it in my ears. It'll clear by evening.

beats.text: You're Marchetti. I read about your Karsten Wall. I heard the radio calls. I heard you need a translator to lead a team.

beats.text: She's standing right here, Hesk. Say it to her.

beats.text: I am saying it to her.

beats.text: You want to know how a deaf woman leads a mountain.

beats.text: I want to know how you hear a falling serac.

beats.text: I don't hear it. I feel it before it falls. Keep up. The porters are already at camp.

scenes.title: Base Camp, flags snapping over orange tents

beats.text: Nima takes Ilse's hand in both of his. Dawa laughs before anyone has said anything worth laughing at.
beats.html: Nima takes Ilse's hand in both of his. Dawa laughs before anyone has said anything worth laughing at.

beats.speaker: dawa
beats.text: You walked fast. Nima said you would. He said the leader walks fast, the team follows, nobody complains.
beats.html: You walked fast. Nima said you would. He said the leader walks fast, the team follows, nobody complains.

beats.speaker: nima
beats.text: The mountain is quiet today. Too quiet. It is waiting.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: It can wait.

beats.speaker: dawa
beats.text: He likes you already. Says you have good feet. Good feet beat good ears. Ears lie. Feet don't.

beats.text: I complain. Put that in the record.

scenes.label: ch_01_s03
scenes.title: Base Camp, inside the mess tent

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: Summit, day six, if the weather holds. The icefall is the only gate the mountain has. We go through it in the dark, before the sun loosens the seracs. Nobody talks in the icefall. You watch my rope and my hand.
beats.html: Summit, day six, if the weather holds. The icefall is the only gate the mountain has. We go through it in the dark, before the sun loosens the seracs. Nobody talks in the icefall. You watch my rope and my hand.

beats.speaker: priya_rask
beats.text: And the bell?
beats.html: And the bell?

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: Below the summit, in a cave of ice the old accounts describe. A bronze bell, about fifteen kilos. History says a guide named Karel Vasek rang it all night in 1908.
beats.html: Below the summit, in a cave of ice the old accounts describe. A bronze bell, about fifteen kilos. History says a guide named Karel Vasek rang it all night in 1908.

beats.speaker: priya_rask
beats.text: That's the account in every book.
beats.html: That's the account in every book.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: The bell is worth nothing but its story. You'll get your photographs. Then we move fast, because the window does not wait for history.
beats.html: The bell is worth nothing but its story. You'll get your photographs. Then we move fast, because the window does not wait for history.

beats.text: The dated photograph shows a bronze bell hanging from an iron bar, and beside it a wooden case with iron corners. Someone has written 1908 on the back in faded pencil.
beats.html: The dated photograph shows a bronze bell hanging from an iron bar, and beside it a wooden case with iron corners. Someone has written 1908 on the back in faded pencil.

beats.speaker: hesk_vandry
beats.text: Let me say the thing nobody's saying. Six expeditions failed. Two people died of altitude. And now we go up with a leader who can't hear a radio?
beats.html: Let me say the thing nobody's saying. Six expeditions failed. Two people died of altitude. And now we go up with a leader who can't hear a radio?

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: I have a light. Red, amber, green. Teodor calls the weather from below and I read the light. On the rope we use tugs. Two, stop. Three, climb. One long pull, danger, anchor now.
beats.html: I have a light. Red, amber, green. Teodor calls the weather from below and I read the light. On the rope we use tugs. Two, stop. Three, climb. One long pull, danger, anchor now.

beats.speaker: hesk_vandry
beats.text: And if you can't feel the rope because your hands are cold?
beats.html: And if you can't feel the rope because your hands are cold?

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: My hands are never that cold. Ask your questions here, not at six thousand metres.
beats.html: My hands are never that cold. Ask your questions here, not at six thousand metres.

beats.speaker: hesk_vandry
beats.text: Then here's one. A week's pay. Before we leave the icefall, you'll call a crevasse that isn't there. Because the ground lies, and you trust your feet.
beats.html: Then here's one. A week's pay. Before we leave the icefall, you'll call a crevasse that isn't there. Because the ground lies, and you trust your feet.

beats.speaker: teodor_brann
beats.text: That's enough.
beats.html: That's enough.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: One week's pay. Agreed. And a second stake. If I call a real one before you hear it, you wear my rope and you don't argue the signals for the rest of the climb.
beats.html: One week's pay. Agreed. And a second stake. If I call a real one before you hear it, you wear my rope and you don't argue the signals for the rest of the climb.

beats.speaker: hesk_vandry
beats.text: Deal.
beats.html: Deal.

beats.text: They don't shake. Nima watches Hesk the way a hawk watches weather. Dawa quietly sets a mug back on a corner of the map.
beats.html: They don't shake. Nima watches Hesk the way a hawk watches weather. Dawa quietly sets a mug back on a corner of the map.

scenes.label: ch_01_s04
scenes.title: Base Camp, at the edge of the tents

beats.text: Ilse finds him alone, watching the summit. She crouches and lays one palm on the rock. He crouches too, mocking it.
beats.html: Ilse finds him alone, watching the summit. She crouches and lays one palm on the rock. He crouches too, mocking it.

beats.speaker: hesk_vandry
beats.text: What is that?
beats.html: What is that?

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: The icefall is moving. Not fast. The glacier is a river that never stops. When the seracs shift, it goes through the rock. You hear it with your ears when it's close. I feel it with my feet when it's far.
beats.html: The icefall is moving. Not fast. The glacier is a river that never stops. When the seracs shift, it goes through the rock. You hear it with your ears when it's close. I feel it with my feet when it's far.

beats.speaker: hesk_vandry
beats.text: It's stronger here.
beats.html: It's stronger here.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: That stone sits on a thin crust over a hollow. It carries the vibration farther. In the morning we check everything, together. And Hesk. The bet was a good way to ask your question. Next time, just ask.

scenes.title: Ilvar Range, on the glacier above the moraine

beats.speaker: teodor_brann
beats.text: What?
beats.html: What?

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: The hollow one. Under there. Three metres.
beats.html: The hollow one. Under there. Three metres.

beats.text: She sets her bare palm on the snow. The surface feels thin and drumlike, a resonance rising through her hand.
beats.html: She sets her bare palm on the snow. The surface feels thin and drumlike, a resonance rising through her hand.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: Nima. Probe.
beats.html: Nima. Probe.

beats.text: The probe goes down through the crust, then falls the length of the man's arm. Nima pulls it back, the tip black and wet.
beats.html: The probe goes down through the crust, then falls the length of the man's arm. Nima pulls it back, the tip black and wet.

beats.text: Crevasse. Open under the bridge. We cross there. Solid.
beats.html: Crevasse. Open under the bridge. We cross there. Solid.

beats.text: They cross one at a time on the anchored rope. On the far side, the rope goes taut toward Hesk, then slack, then two tugs, then three. Climb. They climb.

beats.speaker: teodor_brann
beats.text: The boy's quiet. Quiet's a good start.
beats.html: The boy's quiet. Quiet's a good start.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: He hasn't paid anybody anything yet. He still thinks I'm lucky.
beats.html: He hasn't paid anybody anything yet. He still thinks I'm lucky.

beats.text: Ilse tugs the rope three times, and the whole line moves on up into the cold.
beats.html: Ilse tugs the rope three times, and the whole line moves on up into the cold.

scenes.label: ch_01_s06
scenes.title: Ilvar Range, at the foot of the icefall

beats.text: Halfway up the step, Ilse stops dead. She lays her fingers on the blue face of ice.
beats.html: Halfway up the step, Ilse stops dead. She lays her fingers on the blue face of ice.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: It's moving. Ice against ice. Faster now. I don't like the shape of it.
beats.html: It's moving. Ice against ice. Faster now. I don't like the shape of it.

beats.text: She tugs the rope once, long and slow. Four anchors bite into the snow. Hesk pulls once, a question. She doesn't answer.
beats.html: She tugs the rope once, long and slow. Four anchors bite into the snow. Hesk pulls once, a question. She doesn't answer.

beats.text: The pillar leans. She looks up, then back down the line, and points up and to the right. Her fist goes up. Hold.
beats.html: The pillar leans. She looks up, then back down the line, and points up and to the right. Her fist goes up. Hold.

beats.text: The serac comes down in a wall of blue-green, slow, then all at once, and strikes the snow to their left.
beats.html: The serac comes down in a wall of blue-green, slow, then all at once, and strikes the snow to their left.

beats.text: Debris sweeps over the track they walked ten minutes before. Ilse keeps her fist up until the ice settles.
beats.html: Debris sweeps over the track they walked ten minutes before. Ilse keeps her fist up until the ice settles.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: Climb.
beats.html: Climb.

beats.speaker: priya_rask
beats.text: That could have killed us. We didn't hear anything.
beats.html: That could have killed us. We didn't hear anything.

beats.speaker: teodor_brann
beats.text: You don't hear a serac fall until it's fallen. Even with ears. It's the dust that kills you. It comes faster than the ice.
beats.html: You don't hear a serac fall until it's fallen. Even with ears. It's the dust that kills you. It comes faster than the ice.

beats.speaker: nima
beats.text: The rattle above us is not finished. More loose ice on the right of the step.
beats.html: The rattle above us is not finished. More loose ice on the right of the step.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: We take the left line and we take it slow.
beats.html: We take the left line and we take it slow.

beats.speaker: hesk_vandry
beats.text: You felt that before it fell. In your feet. Everyone felt it after. But you felt it before. I owe you a week's pay.
beats.html: You felt that before it fell. In your feet. Everyone felt it after. But you felt it before. I owe you a week's pay.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: You owe me a rope to wear. And no arguing the signals.
beats.html: You owe me a rope to wear. And no arguing the signals.

beats.speaker: teodor_brann
beats.text: And to stand there and watch us all keep our heads. That's what a team is.
beats.html: And to stand there and watch us all keep our heads. That's what a team is.

scenes.label: ch_02_s01
scenes.title: Ilvar Range, the high bowl below the summit shoulder

beats.text: Ilse stops. She turns her face up and presses two fingers under her jaw, then against her cheekbone.
beats.html: Ilse stops. She turns her face up and presses two fingers under her jaw, then against her cheekbone.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: The pressure is turning. It presses on my face like a hand.
beats.html: The pressure is turning. It presses on my face like a hand.

beats.speaker: teodor_brann
beats.text: How long?
beats.html: How long?

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: An hour. Maybe less. We halt at the névé slope and dig.
beats.html: An hour. Maybe less. We halt at the névé slope and dig.

beats.speaker: hesk_vandry
beats.text: Dig what?
beats.html: Dig what?

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: A hole to live in.
beats.html: A hole to live in.

beats.text: The light dulls. The cloud comes down off the summit in a silent wall, and the world goes white from the top down.

beats.speaker: teodor_brann
beats.text: Cut! Cut there!
beats.html: Cut! Cut there!

beats.html: His word reaches Ilse only as the shape of his mouth and a shudder through the snow. She nods and drives her axe in.

beats.text: Swap. Keep digging.
beats.html: Swap. Keep digging.

beats.speaker: priya_rask
beats.text: I'm fine.
beats.html: I'm fine.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: You're not. Swap.
beats.html: You're not. Swap.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: Roof. Smooth it. Doorway there.

scenes.title: Ilvar Range, inside the snow cave

beats.text: Ilse sets her palm flat on the ice floor. The storm's pressure comes up through her seat bones and into her spine.
beats.html: Ilse sets her palm flat on the ice floor. The storm's pressure comes up through her seat bones and into her spine.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: The drift is holding. The roof will last.
beats.html: The drift is holding. The roof will last.

beats.speaker: nima
beats.text: For now.
beats.html: For now.

beats.text: Priya counts the fuel canisters aloud. Twice. The same answer both times.
beats.html: Priya counts the fuel canisters aloud. Twice. The same answer both times.

beats.speaker: priya_rask
beats.text: Four full, two half. That is what we have.

beats.text: Then we have two days. Maybe three.

beats.text: Breach! Pack it!
beats.html: Breach! Pack it!

scenes.title: Ilvar Range

beats.speaker: nima
beats.text: Two cards short. The game still works. Mostly.
beats.html: Two cards short. The game still works. Mostly.

beats.speaker: hesk_vandry
beats.text: You are cheating.
beats.html: You are cheating.

beats.speaker: dawa
beats.text: I do not cheat. I am simply better.

beats.text: You are carrying a lucky stone. That's the only explanation.

beats.text: I carry no stone.

beats.text: I do not like this one.

beats.speaker: priya_rask
beats.text: You have been in storms worse than this.

beats.text: I have been in storms where I could not see my own glove. That is not what I do not like. Tell her what the mountain is doing.

beats.text: Will it come down?

beats.text: Maybe. Not while the snow falls like this. When the snow stops, it will move, or it will not. There is nothing to be done in this snow. So we sit, and we wait, and we do not spend ourselves.

beats.text: You always know, don't you. What the mountain is doing.

beats.text: Told us what?

beats.text: You are paying for this? All of it?

scenes.title: The Ridge of Echoes

scenes.title: The Ridge of Echoes, the long hour

beats.text: One, two, three, four. Rest. One, two, three, four.

scenes.label: ch_06_s05
scenes.title: The Ridge of Echoes, Nima arrives

beats.html: I came up.

beats.text: Your head. It was full of loud water at the col.

scenes.label: ch_06_s06
scenes.title: The Ridge of Echoes, the descent begins

beats.text: Not this evening.

scenes.label: ch_06_s07
scenes.title: Ilvar Range, the ridge above the icefall

beats.text: Nima goes first with a probe and a long step and a short one, tapping ahead like a blind man in his own house. Ilse goes second with her feet reading the ice through her soles.
beats.html: Nima goes first with a probe and a long step and a short one, tapping ahead like a blind man in his own house. Ilse goes second with her feet reading the ice through her soles.

scenes.title: Ilvar Range, inside the changed icefall

beats.text: The litter goes where you go.

scenes.title: Ilvar Range, the second terrace of the icefall

beats.text: Ilse comes down the step and puts her hand under Priya's arm.
beats.html: Ilse comes down the step and puts her hand under Priya's arm.

beats.speaker: ilse_marchetti
beats.text: Up. We are not stopping on the terrace.

beats.text: No. I mean, yes. But.

beats.text: I have to say it before we get down. Before base camp. Before any of them.

beats.text: Then I will be the one to tell it.

scenes.title: Ilvar Range, the last terrace below the icefall

beats.ch01.s04.b006: That stone sits on a thin crust over a hollow. It carries the vibration farther. In the morning we check everything, together. And Hesk. The bet was a good way to ask your question. Next time, just ask.
beats.ch01.s05.b003: The hollow one. Under there. Three metres.
beats.ch01.s05.b004: She sets her bare palm on the snow. The surface feels thin and drumlike, a resonance rising through her hand.
beats.ch01.s05.b006: The probe goes down through the crust, then falls the length of the man's arm. Nima pulls it back, the tip black and wet.
beats.ch01.s05.b007: Crevasse. Open under the bridge. We cross there. Solid.
beats.ch01.s05.b008: They cross one at a time on the anchored rope. On the far side, the rope goes taut toward Hesk, then slack, then two tugs, then three. Climb. They climb.
beats.ch01.s05.b009: The boy's quiet. Quiet's a good start.
beats.ch01.s05.b010: He hasn't paid anybody anything yet. He still thinks I'm lucky.
beats.ch01.s05.b011: Ilse tugs the rope three times, and the whole line moves on up into the cold.
beats.ch01.s06.b002: Halfway up the step, Ilse stops dead. She lays her fingers on the blue face of ice.
beats.ch01.s06.b003: It's moving. Ice against ice. Faster now. I don't like the shape of it.
beats.ch01.s06.b004: She tugs the rope once, long and slow. Four anchors bite into the snow. Hesk pulls once, a question. She doesn't answer.
beats.ch01.s06.b005: The pillar leans. She looks up, then back down the line, and points up and to the right. Her fist goes up. Hold.
beats.ch01.s06.b006: The serac comes down in a wall of blue-green, slow, then all at once, and strikes the snow to their left.
beats.ch01.s06.b007: Debris sweeps over the track they walked ten minutes before. Ilse keeps her fist up until the ice settles.
beats.ch01.s06.b009: That could have killed us. We didn't hear anything.
beats.ch01.s06.b010: You don't hear a serac fall until it's fallen. Even with ears. It's the dust that kills you. It comes faster than the ice.
beats.ch01.s06.b011: The rattle above us is not finished. More loose ice on the right of the step.
beats.ch01.s06.b012: We take the left line and we take it slow.
beats.ch01.s06.b013: You felt that before it fell. In your feet. Everyone felt it after. But you felt it before. I owe you a week's pay.
beats.ch01.s06.b014: You owe me a rope to wear. And no arguing the signals.
beats.ch01.s06.b015: And to stand there and watch us all keep our heads. That's what a team is.
beats.ch02.s01.b002: Ilse stops. She turns her face up and presses two fingers under her jaw, then against her cheekbone.
beats.ch02.s01.b003: The pressure is turning. It presses on my face like a hand.
beats.ch02.s01.b005: An hour. Maybe less. We halt at the névé slope and dig.
beats.ch02.s01.b008: The light dulls. The cloud comes down off the summit in a silent wall, and the world goes white from the top down.
beats.ch02.s02.b003: His word reaches Ilse only as the shape of his mouth and a shudder through the snow. She nods and drives her axe in.
beats.ch02.s02.b004: Priya's gloves go stiff and useless. Ilse pulls a spare pair of mitts from her jacket and pushes them into her hands.
beats.ch02.s02.b008: Priya swaps and digs again, saying nothing. Nima and Dawa fall into an easy rhythm on the two flanks, the rhythm of men who have dug a hundred shelters.
beats.ch02.s02.b009: Hesk swings his shovel like a man proving something to the snow. The snow takes no notice.
beats.ch02.s02.b011: They smooth the roof, cut a doorway, and plug the wind with a bag of gear and a spare rope. Inside, six people breathing warm the air fast. It smells of wet wool, hot metal and fear.
beats.ch02.s03.b002: Ilse sets her palm flat on the ice floor. The storm's pressure comes up through her seat bones and into her spine.
beats.ch02.s03.b003: The drift is holding. The roof will last.
beats.ch02.s03.b005: Priya counts the fuel canisters aloud. Twice. The same answer both times.
beats.ch02.s03.b006: Four full, two half. That is what we have.
beats.ch02.s03.b007: Then we have two days. Maybe three.
beats.ch02.s03.b008: Dawa falls asleep sitting up, chin on his chest. Nima shifts his legs without waking him so his shoulder comes to rest against the wall of snow.
beats.ch02.s03.b009: Near evening the storm tears a corner off the roof. White pours in.
beats.ch02.s03.b011: Priya holds the headlamp. Ilse and Teodor pack the gap. Hesk passes blocks of cut snow like a man feeding a fire. Nobody speaks; there is no point.
beats.ch02.s03.b012: The second morning repeats the first. Same roar, same pressure on the roof, same grey light leaking through the plugged door.
beats.ch02.s04.b002: Two cards short. The game still works. Mostly.
beats.ch02.s04.b004: I do not cheat. I am simply better.
beats.ch02.s04.b005: You are carrying a lucky stone. That's the only explanation.
beats.ch02.s04.b007: The dignity is so total that everyone laughs. The laughter makes the shelter feel smaller and warmer than it is. Then it runs out, and the day goes on.
beats.ch02.s04.b008: The drift settles with a long soft creak. Ilse signs to Nima. They rise and pack the roof with three more blocks. It holds. They sit again.
beats.ch02.s04.b009: I do not like this one.
beats.ch02.s04.b010: You have been in storms worse than this.
beats.ch02.s04.b011: I have been in storms where I could not see my own glove. That is not what I do not like. Tell her what the mountain is doing.
beats.ch02.s04.b012: Under the storm there is another sound. A grinding, high up above the shelf. It started yesterday. It is getting louder. That is not the storm. That is the slope above us moving on its own bed.
beats.ch02.s04.b014: Maybe. Not while the snow falls like this. When the snow stops, it will move, or it will not. There is nothing to be done in this snow. So we sit, and we wait, and we do not spend ourselves.
beats.ch02.s04.b015: You always know, don't you. What the mountain is doing.
beats.ch02.s04.b016: Not always. Often. I would know what you are carrying. Not the cases. The other thing.
beats.ch02.s04.b017: Priya goes still. Her hands find her pack and hold it against her chest.
beats.ch02.s05.b002: I should have told you before we left.
beats.ch02.s05.b004: The money. The funding. It is not the archive's money. Not mostly. The archive put in a little for equipment and permits. The rest is mine. My savings, and a loan against my flat.
beats.ch02.s05.b005: You are paying for this? All of it?
beats.ch02.s05.b006: Two years of research. Four months of grant letters that all came back no. Nobody funds a correction. Nobody funds a plaque being wrong. So I did.
beats.ch02.s05.b007: That is a great deal of money for a plaque.
beats.ch02.s05.b008: It is not for the plaque. It is for the plaque to come down. And for what goes in its place. The truth fits like a key in a lock, and the lock has been shut for a hundred and eighteen years. I am the only one with the key.
beats.ch02.s05.b009: Nobody funds a correction. So I sold my quiet and my savings and I paid. And I did not tell you, because once it was said you would look at me the way you are looking at me now.
beats.ch02.s05.b010: It does not change the mountain. A rope does not care who paid for it. The bell does not care.
beats.ch02.s05.b011: Priya puts her face in her hands. Teodor reaches across the gear and lays his big glove on her shoulder.
beats.ch02.s05.b012: That is the trouble with a lie. You tell it because you fear the people you tell it to. Then you find they are all right, and the lie is the only thing that was not.
beats.ch02.s05.b013: You should have trusted us with it.
beats.ch02.s05.b014: Nobody answers him. He sets his cup down and does not pick it up again.
beats.ch02.s05.b015: The bell is a bronze bell in a cave. What does it have to do with your money?
beats.ch02.s05.b016: Everything. The man on the plaque, Karel Vasek, rang the bell all night, every book says so. It is not true. A cook rang it. A deaf cook, named Anders Weiss, hiring on because a deaf man did not complain about the noise of the wind at night.
beats.ch02.s05.b017: Ilse does not move. Her palm stays flat on the ice.
beats.ch02.s05.b018: He rang it in four strikes and a pause, from midnight until dawn, and the six men who lived lived because of it. Vasek lay in a tent with a broken shoulder and a frozen face and never rang a thing. And when it was over, the credit went to the famous guide, and the cook went down in the record as the man who rang too late.
beats.ch02.s05.b020: For a hundred and eighteen years. My great-great-grandfather died in a poorhouse in a valley town with no plaque, no portrait, no name on any wall. My family carried it. We did not speak of him. We spoke of Vasek, because the world did, and it was easier to be ashamed of the cook quietly.
beats.ch02.s05.b021: So you climb for a cook.
beats.ch02.s05.b022: I climb to give him back his night. That is what all of it is for. The money, the cave, the bell. The book in the cave is his. I know it. And I mean to bring it home and read it out in the east hall under the painting, and make them take the painting down.
beats.ch02.s05.b023: The stove ticks. The storm presses on the roof. Nobody says anything for a while.
beats.ch02.s05.b024: Then we bring it out whole. All of it. Finish your tea. Tomorrow we see what the mountain has done.
beats.ch02.s06.b002: Ilse goes a little way from the shelter, kneels, and lays both palms on the wind-scoured crust.
beats.ch02.s06.b003: The grinding is still there. High up above the shelf. It did not stop in the storm, and it did not come down. It is waiting on its bed.
beats.ch02.s06.b004: The slope above the shelf. The one we have to go under.
beats.ch02.s06.b006: Then we go up fast and light, and we do not linger. And we watch the ground.
beats.ch02.s06.b007: Nima signs slowly, and Teodor speaks for the rest.
beats.ch02.s06.b008: His head filled with a loud water in the night. He cannot trust his balance on the icefall. He will take Dawa and go down by the way we came, this morning, while the snow is set. He will wait for us at the col with the radio and the spare fuel.
beats.ch02.s06.b009: You are right to go. I will see you at the col.
beats.ch02.s06.b010: Dawa shoulders both their loads without being asked. Ilse watches them down the first slope until the ridge takes them. The rope behind her loses two of its voices. She makes herself turn around.
beats.ch02.s07.b002: Ilse holds up her fist. The stop signal travels down the rope and back up again, clean and quick.
beats.ch02.s07.b003: She walks forward alone and presses both palms flat on the bridge. She waits.
beats.ch02.s07.b004: Hollow. And under the hollow, a grinding. The middle is a skin.
beats.ch02.s07.b005: She walks her hands along the arc. At the centre they stop. Through her palms comes a faint gravelly trickle, snow shifting down into the dark.
beats.ch02.s07.b006: She takes her hands away and walks back to the line.
beats.ch02.s07.b008: The bridge is bad. The middle is a skin. Not much left under it.
beats.ch02.s07.b010: Roped, spaced, crawling, belayed from both sides. Or we go around. There is rock on the far side and a step. We go around.
beats.ch02.s07.b011: It is a bridge on the only easy route up the mountain. Every party for a hundred years has crossed something like it.
beats.ch02.s07.b012: Every party for a hundred years has been one storm away from a burial. We go around.
beats.ch02.s07.b013: Hesk steps up to the bridge edge himself. He lays one hand on the snow, the way he has watched her do it, and holds it there.
beats.ch02.s07.b015: Not with the hand. With the ear in the bone. Take your glove off and press harder.
beats.ch02.s07.b016: He pulls his glove off, presses his bare palm to the snow, and frowns. Then his whole face changes.
beats.ch02.s07.b017: It is humming. Like a drum with nobody playing it.
beats.ch02.s07.b018: Now you know what a bad one feels like. Now you wear my rope to the step and you do not argue the signals.
beats.ch02.s07.b019: I paid the week's pay in my head already. I will pay it in money at the bottom.
beats.ch02.s08.b002: Ilse belays from below and watches his feet find the holds. He climbs more carefully than she has seen him climb before.
beats.ch02.s08.b003: He comes down onto safe snow and tugs the rope three times, steady. Then a fourth.
beats.ch02.s08.b004: The fourth tug means nothing. I think he knows it.
beats.ch02.s08.b005: The fourth tug travels up the line to her hands. She pulls twice in answer. He grins, embarrassed, and turns away.
beats.ch02.s08.b006: Priya comes across last and slowly, and stands with her hands on her knees.
beats.ch02.s08.b007: That cost us time. An hour and a half, at least.
beats.ch02.s08.b008: It cost us the margin. We go anyway.
beats.ch02.s08.b009: Beyond the step the ground flattens beneath a hanging slope, and the light is going.
beats.ch02.s09.b002: She feels the grinding, no more than a stone's throw up the slope, moving against its bed in small steps, the way a door moves before it opens.
beats.ch02.s09.b003: Teodor comes and stands beside her. She keeps her hands where they are for a while. Then she takes them away.
beats.ch02.s09.b005: In the dark, before the sun loads it. Fast. We do not stop under the crest, not for the view, not for the rope, not for anybody's bootlace. And we tell them tonight.
beats.ch02.s09.b006: They tell them in the tent, over the stove. Four faces take it.
beats.ch02.s09.b007: The bridge. Going around cost us the margin, didn't it.
beats.ch02.s09.b008: It did. We are going anyway. The crossing is made in the dark.
beats.ch02.s09.b009: Priya asks nothing. Her hands lie folded on her pack, and her eyes stay on Ilse's face.
beats.ch02.s09.b011: The cutter. In my pack. The small one. I told you it was for the document boards. It is for the page. The first page. If it is there.
beats.ch02.s09.b012: You mean to cut it out.
beats.ch02.s09.b013: I mean to take his name out of it. With the cutter if the fire was too slow. So that at least nobody reads it and knows him for a liar. I have known since the city that I would.
beats.ch02.s09.b015: Then the storm came, and you put your hand on my shoulder, and I could not say it in the snow cave with all of you looking. I am saying it now. Before the slope. In case there is no after.
beats.ch02.s09.b016: You will bring it out whole. Both of us will. And the bell. And the page. That is the promise of the dark crossing.
beats.ch02.s09.b017: I do not trust myself to keep it.
beats.ch02.s09.b018: Then I will keep it for you until you can.
beats.ch02.s09.b019: Ilse puts out her hand. Priya takes it, briefly, and lets go.
beats.ch02.s10.b002: They go at four, fast and spaced, no stops. Halfway across, the ground under Ilse's right boot gives a small, terrible sigh.
beats.ch02.s10.b003: She drops onto both palms without being told. The whole slope waits. She holds. It holds. She gets up and goes on.
beats.ch02.s10.b004: Past the crest the ground smooths and opens into the long white shelf. She does not let herself look back until her boots are on flat, hard snow. Then she counts the rope four times over. Every one of them.
beats.ch02.s10.b005: Ilse. The barometer is falling. Two days, maybe less. Do not linger up there.
beats.ch02.s11.b002: Ilse gives the rock beside the mouth a long time. The mountain's deep pulse is in it, slow and heavy. Under the pulse, faint and fine, something is ringing like a wire strung tight.
beats.ch02.s11.b003: Listen. Not with the ears. Put your hands here.
beats.ch02.s11.b004: Hesk kneels and presses both bare palms to the rock. He is still for a while.
beats.ch02.s11.b005: There is something in it. Something small. Like a bell that has already rung and not stopped.
beats.ch02.s11.b006: The mouth is plugged with a hundred winters of ice. We cut it at first light, all four of us in turns.
beats.ch02.s11.b008: Is not going to wait for another evening. A long cut at the plug is a long time under it. We take the morning to read what we can from outside, and we cut. If the mountain moves again, we go down without it. The window is the window.
beats.ch02.s11.b009: Priya stands at the mouth with her hands on the ice, and says nothing, and will not look away from it.
beats.ch03.s01.b002: Ilse stands a moment with her weight on both feet and feels the mountain through the soles of her boots. Something thin and high went through her shoulder blade an hour before the alarm. It has not come again.
beats.ch03.s01.b003: The mountain spoke in the night. Once. It will not say it twice. We move now.
beats.ch03.s01.b004: The slope is still there, then.
beats.ch03.s01.b005: It is still there. That is why we cross it before the sun touches it.
beats.ch03.s01.b006: She counts them on the rope with her hand, four times over. Then she turns and leads up into the dark.
beats.ch03.s02.b002: Ilse kneels in front of Nima so he can see her hands. She signs slowly. He watches her fingers, and signs back.
beats.ch03.s02.b003: My head is full of loud water. I cannot trust my feet on the icefall.
beats.ch03.s02.b004: Then you are right to go down. I will see you at the col. Keep the radio warm.
beats.ch03.s02.b005: She lays her hand flat on his shoulder. He grips it once, hard, and lets go.
beats.ch03.s02.b006: I take him down by the way we came, while the snow is set. We wait at the col with the radio and the spare fuel. You come down and we go home.
beats.ch03.s02.b007: Take the spare canisters. We can cut our fuel if we must.
beats.ch03.s02.b008: We have enough. Walk careful, all of you. The mountain is talking and it does not like to repeat itself.
beats.ch03.s02.b009: Dawa shoulders both their loads. The two of them go down the first slope, slow and sure, and the ridge takes them from sight.
beats.ch03.s03.b002: The cold no longer bites. It presses. The four of them go quiet together, unprompted. Priya's breathing grows loud and ragged in the thin air.
beats.ch03.s03.b004: Like a hand on the chest. Everyone feels it. Tell them to breathe slow and not to fight it.
beats.ch03.s03.b005: He turns and passes it down the line. Priya nods and makes herself breathe slower. Hesk does not look up.
beats.ch03.s04.b002: The surface rings a little under her weight, a thin crust with something soft beneath it. She does not like it, and she says so.
beats.ch03.s04.b003: It is loaded above a soft band. We cross fast and spaced. Nobody stops under the crest. Not for a bootlace, not for a view.
beats.ch03.s04.b005: It starts under the feet before it moves. I will tell you. Hesk, you are second. Priya, keep the rope snug and your eyes up.
beats.ch03.s04.b006: What does it feel like? Before it moves.
beats.ch03.s04.b007: Like a deep slow rising in the boots. You will not miss it. Go.
beats.ch03.s04.b008: They go. Halfway across, the ground speaks.
beats.ch03.s05.b002: Ilse drives her axe to the head, drops her weight, and strikes the snow with her palm. Three hard beats. The ground, the ground, the ground.
beats.ch03.s05.b003: The beats! That is her. That is the ground talking!
beats.ch03.s05.b004: She signs at Hesk with a face he cannot mistake. Down. Anchor now. Hesk has climbed toward a jut of rock out from under the crest. He sees her hands and does not come down.
beats.ch03.s05.b006: Teodor drives his axe in, puts his weight on the hump, and hauls the rope tight. Hesk moves because Teodor moves. Priya moves because the rope pulls her.
beats.ch03.s05.b007: It opens along a crack a hundred metres wide. The snow lifts as though something under it has drawn breath. Then the whole slab comes off and comes down.
beats.ch03.s05.b008: White fills the world. The rope jerks. She takes the pull through her shoulders and her heels and lies with her cheek on her arm, counting. One. Two. Three. The hump holds. The river of white pours past below them and falls away into the bowl.
beats.ch03.s05.b009: The roar goes on, and then it stops. The silence that follows is so complete she carries it on her back.
beats.ch03.s05.b010: She tugs once. The answer comes back up the line. One, two, three. She digs them out and checks them with her hands, because her voice cannot reach Teodor's deaf side in that wind.
beats.ch03.s05.b011: I am whole. A cut on the cheek. Nothing.
beats.ch03.s05.b012: It came over us. I felt it go past. It was so fast.
beats.ch03.s05.b013: Teodor has a red line down his cheek. Thirty metres wide of them, the slab has buried the traverse completely.
beats.ch03.s05.b014: Everybody up. Hands and feet and faces. Hesk, Priya's face. Teodor, my back.
beats.ch03.s06.b002: Hesk turns on her. His voice has gone high and raw.
beats.ch03.s06.b003: Reckless. That is what that was. One metre more and it would have taken us. You saw nothing. You called it on a feeling in your feet.
beats.ch03.s06.b004: Quiet. Quiet is the one thing that can reach you now. Listen to me.
beats.ch03.s06.b006: The crossing began eleven minutes ago. It takes fifty to be clear of the hanging slope. I called it at the end of the soft snow, where I could call it. You were off the rope, under the crest, and you would not come down until Teodor hauled you. That is the recklessness on this hump. It is not mine.
beats.ch03.s06.b007: I could not feel it. The way you do.
beats.ch03.s06.b008: That is not the failing. The failing is that you did not come down when I told you to come down.
beats.ch03.s06.b009: Listen to me, boy. I have climbed with this woman nineteen years. I have seen her call weather the forecasters missed, and ice that would have killed us all. I have never once seen her guess.
beats.ch03.s06.b011: She pinned you to the hump and you asked her twice before you moved. Take your accusation down that rope quietly, or I will tie you off and leave you for the mountain.
beats.ch03.s06.b012: Hesk looks at his boots. The wind moves the dust between them.
beats.ch03.s06.b014: They climb off the hump and up the far side of the slide, spaced and quiet. Priya comes up last, and Ilse waits for her and checks the rope at her waist with her hands.
beats.ch03.s07.b002: That is the cave. We are where the grid puts it.
beats.ch03.s07.b003: They cross in the flat hard light. Ilse stops them a little way from the rock and has Priya come up beside her.
beats.ch03.s07.b004: You have carried that pack through the storm and past the slide. What is in it?
beats.ch03.s07.b005: Archive materials. Protective cases, handling gloves, a small cutter, the document boards. The archive made me promise to do it correctly.
beats.ch03.s07.b007: For the boards. If the book is there it must not be handled bare. That is the archive rule.
beats.ch03.s07.b008: Priya turns away. Ilse waits. Priya stands very still with her hands on the pack.
beats.ch03.s07.b009: It is for the page. The first page. I told myself I came here to correct the record. I have begun to think I came here to bury it. That is all I can say on a shelf in the light.
beats.ch03.s07.b010: I will hold you to the rest of it when there is time to hear it.
beats.ch03.s07.b011: Priya nods once and picks up the pack. They come to the mouth together and look.
beats.ch03.s08.b002: Ilse sets both palms on the plug and holds them there until the others quiet. The cold burns rather than freezes.
beats.ch03.s08.b003: Through the burn comes the deep low pulse of the mountain. Under the pulse is a small stillness, an emptiness where the cave goes back.
beats.ch03.s08.b004: And in that space something shifts that is not the mountain. A vibration all its own, finer than any the rock makes. Like a wire drawn very tight, struck once, left to ring.
beats.ch03.s08.b005: The bell is behind it. I felt the room. And I felt something ringing in it. Small. Old.
beats.ch03.s08.b007: We cut it. It will take all of us in turns, and the window narrows while we cut. Hesk, first shift beside me. Teodor, the lamp and the snow. Priya, the bag and the boards. There is no hour to rest in. We go now.
beats.ch03.s08.b008: Hesk pulls his axe from his belt and goes to the seam.
beats.ch03.s09.b002: The plug does not shatter the way summer ice shatters. It comes away in hard grey chips, and every blow tells Ilse how much thickness still stands between her and the dark.
beats.ch03.s09.b003: Hesk cuts beside her and for a long stretch says nothing. Then, between strokes, with his eyes on the seam, he speaks.
beats.ch03.s09.b004: I could not feel it. On the hump. I have put my hand on the ground a dozen times since and felt nothing at all.
beats.ch03.s09.b005: Most people feel nothing. That is not a failing. It is why we rope up and drill the signals. You moved when Teodor pulled. That is all the mountain asked of you.
beats.ch03.s09.b006: It is not what I said to you.
beats.ch03.s09.b007: No. It is what you are doing now. That is worth more to me than the other.
beats.ch03.s09.b008: A plate of ice comes away and rings on the shelf. Hesk works on, quieter. Teodor takes the second shift and Hesk the third.
beats.ch03.s09.b009: Priya holds the lamp and the bag and takes no turn. Each time the wind blows fine snow into the mouth, she clears it and goes back to watching the seam, and her hands stay hooked in the strap of her pack.
beats.ch03.s10.b002: It smells faintly sweet, and of iron. Ilse puts her face to the hole and cold air comes out against her skin.
beats.ch03.s10.b003: There is a room. Low ceiling. The air has not moved in a hundred years.
beats.ch03.s10.b005: I can feel the ring of it through the rock. It is still inside. Patience. We open it in the morning when we can see what we are doing.
beats.ch03.s10.b006: They pitch the tent on the shelf close under the rock. Teodor stands watch on the north ridge and watches the cloud there, and it is coming down.
beats.ch03.s10.b007: Cloud on the north ridge. Moving fast. We have tonight, perhaps.
beats.ch03.s10.b008: Then we sleep in turns and we are through that hole at first light.
beats.ch03.s10.b009: Priya sets her pack inside the tent, sits with it against her knees, and does not lie down. Hesk lies down and is asleep in a minute. Teodor takes the first watch. Ilse takes the second, and sits with her back to the rock, and feels the small, fine ringing go on and on behind the ice.
beats.ch03.s10.b010: Whatever you are ringing for. We are almost there.
beats.ch04.s01.b002: Ilse comes last out of the tent and stands by the hole a moment, feeling the rock through her boots.
beats.ch04.s01.b003: It is quiet. Too quiet. The wind has gone round to the north.
beats.ch04.s01.b005: They go through the hole one at a time, Priya lit from below by the lamp and climbing like a woman wading into cold water.
beats.ch04.s01.b006: Keep your head down. The ceiling is low.
beats.ch04.s01.b007: I am through. Ilse. Ilse, come and see this.
beats.ch04.s02.b002: The bell's mouth is turned down. The crown is bright with a thin skin of frost where the bronze has not gone green. The bar has taken its weight since 1908.
beats.ch04.s02.b003: Ilse walks to it and lays her hand flat on its side. The bronze meets her palm with a cold like water.
beats.ch04.s02.b004: Nothing. No hum. Not a wire. Just cold.
beats.ch04.s02.b005: Small thing, isn't it. For all that.
beats.ch04.s02.b006: Heavier than it looks. That is the way with bells.
beats.ch04.s02.b007: Behind the bell, against the far wall, a wooden case stands half swallowed by the ice, its lid shut, its lock rusted hard. On the top lies a parcel wrapped in oilskin.
beats.ch04.s02.b008: It is his. The case is his. It has the expedition's mark burned into the lid. The three crosses and the ring.
beats.ch04.s03.b002: The ice comes away in grey chips. Hesk sets the oilskin parcel aside, clears the lock, and Priya works the rust with a bar until it gives.
beats.ch04.s03.b003: The lid comes up. Inside, packed in black wool, lies a second bundle in oilskin hardened to a shell. Three empty bottles. A tin of biscuit. A coil of rope gone to powder at her touch.
beats.ch04.s03.b004: The first page is written in a careful, level hand: the book of Anders Weiss, cook to the expedition of 1908, who cannot hear and who keeps his account in writing, that the truth may be here when the storm is done.
beats.ch04.s03.b006: The evening of the eleventh of September the mountain came down upon the camp.
beats.ch04.s04.b002: The master Vasek was struck in the tent and took harm upon his shoulder and his face, and did not wake. There were seven living and the storm upon us, and no way down and no voice that could carry.
beats.ch04.s04.b003: So I took the bell kept for the signal. I hung it on the iron bar and I rang it through the night. The men came to the sound by threes and by twos. Six lived. One did not.
beats.ch04.s04.b004: I rang until my arms were dead, and then I rang with my feet upon the rope, and the ringing went into the ice, and the ice carried it down the mountain like a road.
beats.ch04.s04.b005: Ilse puts her hand back on the bronze. This time something comes, from the ice under her boots, from the whole shelf and peak, the slow deep pulse of the mountain, and inside it a small struck-wire memory.
beats.ch04.s04.b006: He rang with his feet. He knew the ice would carry it. He spoke to the mountain, not to the air.
beats.ch04.s04.b007: And this. And I will set down here that the master Vasek was a good man and a brave one, and did not know what happened in those hours. But the account that walks down the mountain will be written by men who were not here. So this is my book, and it is the truth, and I leave it in the place of the bell.
beats.ch04.s04.b008: A hundred and eighteen years, waiting in the dark.
beats.ch04.s04.b009: Priya's face has gone loose and bright and close to breaking. Her hands shake on the book.
beats.ch04.s04.b010: Hesk. Put the book back and close the case. We photograph everything now, in place.
beats.ch04.s04.b011: Priya does not move. Her thumb has found the corner of the first page, and the dry paper lifts.
beats.ch04.s05.b002: I cannot. It is not a correction, it is a confession. My family is the shame. He was the cook they blamed, and I have spent my life in the hall that hangs his disgrace on the wall.
beats.ch04.s05.b003: Priya. Step back from the lamp.
beats.ch04.s05.b004: I was going to bury the truth. I told myself I would say the book was too damaged to read.
beats.ch04.s05.b005: She puts the corner of the page into the flame. It catches at once, orange rippling up the leaf, smoke white and thin.
beats.ch04.s05.b006: Hesk crosses the ice in two strides. He does not grab the book. He takes her wrist and pinches the burning corner flat and holds it until no glow is left.
beats.ch04.s05.b007: A bite has gone out of the corner, brown-edged and ragged, the size of a thumbnail. The smoke hangs in the roof in a thin white breath.
beats.ch04.s05.b008: I am sorry. I nearly burned his name out of the world.
beats.ch04.s05.b009: Nearly. The rest is in the case.
beats.ch04.s05.b010: A book that survived a fire is a better witness than one that did not.
beats.ch04.s05.b011: Get the case, Priya. You are the archivist. Pack it like you were taught. I will hold the light.
beats.ch04.s05.b012: Priya kneels and does it. Her hands have steadied. She wraps the book in oilskin and wool, closes the lid, and locks it with the bar, slowly, without a word.
beats.ch04.s06.b002: She photographs the bell where it hangs, the crown letters, the iron bar, the mark of the rope on it. She photographs the case, its lock and mark. She photographs the first page open with its burnt corner black against the ice.
beats.ch04.s06.b003: The bell, then. Three of us and me holding.
beats.ch04.s06.b004: Teodor takes the crown while the others ease it off the iron. It weighs more than fifteen kilos. When they lay it in the rope cradle Ilse has built, mouth down, the cave seems emptier.
beats.ch04.s06.b006: Give it something to say and it will.
beats.ch04.s06.b007: They carry the cradle through the hole. In the white flat afternoon light the bronze takes the sun and holds it, and for a moment it glows as if it were warm.
beats.ch04.s07.b002: The valley answers after a hiss. A man's voice, thin with distance and surprise, asks who is on the channel.
beats.ch04.s07.b003: Base camp, this is Marchetti on the shelf. All four alive. We have the bell and the book. The book is whole but for one scorched corner, scorched today and by our own hand.
beats.ch04.s07.b004: The cook is the man. Anders Weiss rang the bell. His own hand wrote it, and his account is with us.
beats.ch04.s07.b005: The speaker is quiet a moment. Then the man speaks again, slowly, to someone behind him and then to her.
beats.ch04.s07.b006: Say again, Marchetti. Say again the cook.
beats.ch04.s07.b007: His name was Anders Weiss. He was deaf and he was not the man they blamed. He saved six. He wrote it down. We are coming down.
beats.ch04.s07.b008: The valley makes a noise like a room full of hands. Teodor's jaw is tight. He nods at her once.
beats.ch04.s07.b009: Marchetti, the forecast desk holds four days. But I do not trust it. There is cloud from the north the models have not placed, and my barometer has fallen nine millibars since noon. If it comes early you will not get four days. Call me every four hours.
beats.ch04.s07.b010: Four days by the forecast. The mountain has not read the forecast.
beats.ch04.s07.b011: She turns the dial down and wraps the radio in its case.
beats.ch04.s07.b012: I have never liked a radio that agrees with me. Look at the ridge. The far wall. The cloud is down on the north.
beats.ch04.s07.b013: The north ridge has gone grey and soft. The Ridge of Echoes has disappeared into a low whiteness that is not snow but cloud, and the wind is coming with it.
beats.ch04.s07.b014: The mountain says two. Maybe one.
beats.ch04.s07.b015: We leave at first light. We go down through the icefall in the dark, and we carry the bell, and we do not stop until the col.
beats.ch04.s07.b016: The book is in its case. The bell is in its cradle. I am ready, Ilse. All of me, this time.
beats.ch04.s07.b017: The cloud comes down the north wall and takes the ridge, and the shelf goes grey, and the four of them stand in the lee of the rock with the bell between them and the descent still to come.
beats.ch05.s01.b002: Ilse stands with her palm on the shelf rock. The wind turns over in the upper bowl and she feels it turn. The forecast gave four days. Her feet give her two.
beats.ch05.s01.b003: The difference gets counted in hours we do not have. We go at first light.
beats.ch05.s01.b004: Sit down and eat something. You are no good to anyone hungry.
beats.ch05.s01.b006: The bell comes down in the cradle, middle of the line. We go at the pace of the slowest, and the slowest is the bell.
beats.ch05.s01.b007: Priya has sat all night with her hands on the case and has not slept. Hesk repacks, and repacks again, and leaves half of it scattered on the rock.
beats.ch05.s01.b008: I am ready. I am ready.
beats.ch05.s01.b009: Then pick it all up and be ready.
beats.ch05.s02.b002: They make the first hour the good hour. Dry rock, hard snow, the old track still holding under the new. Every fifty metres Ilse calls the line tight, and the ice remembers where they cut it.
beats.ch05.s02.b003: Ilse lays her hand on the bell. Through the bronze and the cradle she feels the terrace, and the ice under it, and the ice is moving.
beats.ch05.s02.b004: The ground is on the move. Slow. Something above has not decided yet.
beats.ch05.s02.b005: Then we do not stand still to argue with it.
beats.ch05.s02.b006: Hesk has stopped with the rear rope slack and his head turned back up the way they came. He comes on, and holds his tongue until the second terrace.
beats.ch05.s03.b004: Fifteen kilos slung between us, and it is going to cost us. I can feel the weight. Slowly is how people die on mountains. You told me that yourself.
beats.ch05.s03.b005: We can cache it. Mark the spot, come back in the spring. It is a bell. It has waited a hundred years.
beats.ch05.s03.b006: That is the best argument you have made since the road. Look down.
beats.ch05.s03.b007: She points into the icefall. The cloud has swallowed the next terrace and is still climbing.
beats.ch05.s03.b008: In an hour that is a whiteout. Then we go by rope and by voice, and a voice carries nowhere in a whiteout. But you can follow a bell. It was rung through a night to bring six men over ice like this. It already knows the way.
beats.ch05.s03.b009: So the bell is a radio, and the radio is dead.
beats.ch05.s03.b010: The radio is not dead yet.
beats.ch05.s03.b011: It will be. Then we are four people in a whiteout carrying a bell, when we could be four people running.
beats.ch05.s03.b012: Four people who can find each other beat four who cannot. We take the bell.
beats.ch05.s03.b013: Hesk holds her eyes, and the snow goes between them. At last he takes up the rear of the cradle.
beats.ch05.s03.b014: Your call. It is your rope.
beats.ch05.s03.b015: That is not the end of the argument. It is only the pause.
beats.ch05.s04.b002: Teodor goes into a hole. Not a crevasse. A hollow under the new snow where a boulder has shifted and left a gap.
beats.ch05.s04.b003: His boot punches through to the knee, his pack swings, and he goes down with the cradle rope still in his fist. Ilse sits hard on the rope. Hesk is on him before she has finished moving.
beats.ch05.s04.b006: Ilse cuts the bootlace and works the boot off. The ankle has swollen to the colour of an old bruise. She feels it front and back with her thumbs.
beats.ch05.s04.b007: Bones are whole. I am almost sure the bones are whole.
beats.ch05.s04.b008: Stand. Put your weight on it.
beats.ch05.s04.b009: He stands, puts his weight on it, and goes straight down with a sound like a sigh.
beats.ch05.s04.b010: That is not a sprain you walk off. A bad ankle and the man rides.
beats.ch05.s04.b011: Nobody rides. I have no litter and we are not building one. I can hop.
beats.ch05.s04.b012: You do not hop five hundred metres of icefall.
beats.ch05.s04.b013: Do not put a rope on me and hang me off your shoulder. You need your shoulder for the bell.
beats.ch05.s04.b014: Ilse wraps the ankle tight with the long bandage, pulls the boot on, and laces until the leather creaks.
beats.ch05.s04.b015: You walk in the middle of the line now. Between Hesk and Priya. One tug for a good step. Two for a bad. Three and we stop.
beats.ch05.s04.b016: That is the slowest pace on the mountain.
beats.ch05.s04.b017: That is the pace. Now walk.
beats.ch05.s05.b002: Ilse stops them, turns them, and crowds them down around the bell. Her feet feel the wind through the ground, a hard high hum, and beneath it the deep irregular counting of the mountain.
beats.ch05.s05.b003: She lays her hands on the bronze. Through it comes the slide of new snow over old slab, running down the grade toward the drop.
beats.ch05.s05.b004: The snow is moving under the cradle.
beats.ch05.s05.b005: Hesk shakes his head and raises his hand in the sign she taught him. Nothing here. Then he shuts one eye and makes a second sign, slow and clear. And on this side the storm is too loud to hear.
beats.ch05.s05.b006: Priya pulls off a glove and lays her bare hand on the wooden case. Her face changes. She grabs Hesk's arm and puts his hand where hers had been, and he needs no words.
beats.ch05.s05.b007: The ground under the case is still. The case is on the old ice of the terrace. The bell is on the moving snow.
beats.ch05.s05.b008: The radio cracks against Ilse's shoulder. She works the dial and gets one more click, and then nothing. She straps it away and marks the promise broken.
beats.ch05.s05.b009: When we miss the fourth hour, they will know. Their knowing will not reach us.
beats.ch05.s05.b010: She gathers them into a huddle and uses her hands on their shoulders, slow and wide. Radio dead. The bell goes on the ridge. Follow the ring.
beats.ch05.s05.b012: They cannot find us in this. They can find the bell. Four hours and the cloud lifts. The icefall will be a mess below. Now.
beats.ch05.s05.b013: We go up on the ridge and we cannot come down the icefall at all. We will be above it with no way down.
beats.ch05.s05.b015: And if we stay here we are on a slope that is already moving.
beats.ch05.s05.b017: He holds her gaze. Then he makes the flat decision sign with his hand, takes the front of the cradle, and looks back at her.
beats.ch05.s05.b018: He has stopped arguing. He has started climbing.
beats.ch05.s06.b002: Teodor goes up on the good leg and brings the bad one after and sobs once between his teeth and goes on. Twice the snow surges under Ilse's boots. Once the whole slope lets go somewhere below in the grey, and she neither hears it nor learns where it went.
beats.ch05.s06.b003: It takes an hour and a half to gain what twenty minutes would give in clear air. Then they come over the last of the slope onto the shoulder.
beats.ch05.s06.b004: The Ridge of Echoes lies along the top of the icefall like a spine. Black ice, packed snow, no cover. The wind comes over it with nothing in the way.
beats.ch05.s07.b002: Ilse runs the line to a piton she drives with four blows and ties Teodor off, then Hesk, then Priya. Then she gets the bell out of the cradle.
beats.ch05.s07.b003: A spine of rock stands up out of the snow at the high point. She finds a crack wide enough for the crown, lays the bronze in, and wedges it with two flat stones.
beats.ch05.s07.b004: She drives a piton above it and ties the crown so it cannot walk away. Then she takes the bar from the cradle's lashing and strikes the bell.
beats.ch05.s07.b005: No sound comes through the air. Her bare hand lies on the rock, and the rock takes the sound and gives it to her, down the ridge and into the frozen mountain in a long slow wave.
beats.ch05.s07.b006: She strikes again and sets the rhythm she learned in the cave. Four slow beats and a rest. Four and a rest. Then she puts the bar into Teodor's hands and lays his palm on the rock until he nods.
beats.ch05.s07.b007: I feel it. Go and rest. I have got it.
beats.ch05.s07.b008: The hours that follow are not hours a person counts. They take the bar in turns and keep the bell ringing, and the world stays folded in grey.
beats.ch05.s08.b002: I lied to all of you.
beats.ch05.s08.b003: I know. You tried to burn the page.
beats.ch05.s08.b004: That is not the lie. I told Ilse I was a woman who had found some papers. I told base camp the archive funded the equipment. It put in a little. The most of it was me.
beats.ch05.s08.b005: My savings and a loan against my flat and a bad arrangement with a man in the city who calls himself a banker. If it failed I would have gone home to nothing.
beats.ch05.s08.b006: I thought that was why I was doing it. So that at the end I could say I paid for the truth and it was expensive and I was brave. That is a lie too. I was doing it so I would not have to read the truth about my own family.
beats.ch05.s08.b007: The guide. Karel Vasek. He was the one with the painting.
beats.ch05.s08.b008: He was the one with the painting. The east hall has him with the bell-rope and his mouth open, singing, coming down out of the sky to save them. He was in a tent with his shoulder broken and his face broken and could not say what day it was.
beats.ch05.s08.b009: Every plaque in my country says his name. And my great-great-grandfather's name is the cook's shame. My mother whispered it. I was not allowed to ask. She taught me to be ashamed of him.
beats.ch05.s08.b010: He rang it all night. With no way up and no way down. Why ring at all, when no one could hear and he could not hear the answer?
beats.ch05.s08.b011: Because it was the only thing he could do.
beats.ch05.s08.b012: Hesk looks down the ridge to where Ilse stands at the bell with the bar in her hands. He gets up and goes along the rope.
beats.ch05.s08.b014: I see it now. You are not calling the mountain. You are asking it where it is going. Weiss did the same. He put the bell in the ice and asked it to carry his voice where he could not.
beats.ch05.s08.b017: Let it stay unpaid. It was a stupid bet.
beats.ch05.s08.b018: Ilse strikes the bell, and they both feel it go down the ridge into the dark, and Hesk gives her the nod he gave her in the icefall.
beats.ch05.s09.b002: Teodor rings first and his hands are good. Ilse lies in the lee where the rock carries the strokes and corrects the rhythm with her palm when it drifts. Then Hesk rings, then Priya, then Ilse again.
beats.ch05.s09.b003: They might not come. Even if they hear. No one can climb in this.
beats.ch05.s09.b004: The valley keeps a clock even when we do not. They will have missed us by now. They will be at the foot of the icefall and they will hear nothing and they will stop and wonder.
beats.ch05.s09.b005: Then one of them will feel the ground go small and tight under his boots. He will put his hand down. He will walk up the mountain to the place it is coming from. The rescue is not a thing you hear. It is a thing you follow.
beats.ch05.s09.b006: We could try the descent. The ridge runs down the east side. If we roped the bell down the east face, slowly, four at a time, we might make the bottom before the worst of the cold.
beats.ch05.s09.b007: If we stay here we freeze. Asking, not arguing. Might is better than sitting.
beats.ch05.s09.b008: Then feel it yourself. Come and put your hand where mine was.
beats.ch05.s09.b009: Hesk goes to the edge, lays his bare hand on the ice through the snow, and stays there a while.
beats.ch05.s09.b010: Loose and grainy. The whole face is sliding against itself. Four hundred feet of a sieve on a face we cannot see. We would be down the first pitch and it would take us, and the bell would be under it.
beats.ch05.s09.b012: He makes the flat decision sign and goes back to the slab and sits down.
beats.ch05.s09.b013: Have you ever been in one that did not end?
beats.ch05.s09.b014: Ilse lets the question sit. She thinks of a sentry line set too late on another mountain, and a partner who did not come home. Then she makes herself look at Priya.
beats.ch05.s09.b015: I have been in one when it ended wrong. The mountain does not tell you which kind it is until the end. So you keep ringing.
beats.ch05.s09.b016: She strikes the bell. Four and a rest. The rock takes it and she feels it go down the ridge and out into the mountain, and somewhere far below, the mountain carries it on.
beats.ch05.s09.b017: Ilse. If it comes down to it. The ringing. You keep it going, you hear me. Not me. You.
beats.ch05.s09.b018: Nobody is leaving anybody on this ridge. Ring your set.
beats.ch05.s09.b019: He rings his set. Four and a rest. The wind takes the sound and the ground keeps it, and the night settles over the Ridge of Echoes with no way down and no radio and four people keeping a sound alive in the ground.
beats.ch06.s01.b002: Ilse counts the dark by the strokes. Four strikes, then a rest. Each set sends her hand a little deeper into the rock.
beats.ch06.s01.b003: This rock has been struck a thousand times. It has never once rung.
beats.ch06.s01.b004: Through her palm she reads where the ridge stands solid and where it rings hollow. Where the ice meets the stone. Where the stone has broken away and hangs.
beats.ch06.s01.b006: I feel the mountain. It does not answer quickly. Keep the pot going and wake us to drink.
beats.ch06.s01.b007: Priya works the stove. Hesk rises without being told and goes out to check the anchor, and Ilse follows him through the floor with her hand.
beats.ch06.s02.b002: The wind is dying. The roar has left it, and what remains is a hiss and a tugging. The storm is spending itself.
beats.ch06.s02.b003: At the east edge of the ridge her hand finds the loose ice face has stopped sliding and firmed again, the way a face does when the wind that worked it rests.
beats.ch06.s02.b004: The east is quiet. Quiet is not safe. Quiet is only quiet.
beats.ch06.s02.b005: She lays her palm on the bronze still wedged in its crack and strikes it once, hard. Then she waits, counting.
beats.ch06.s02.b006: Hesk. Come down. Put your hands where mine are and tell me what you feel.
beats.ch06.s02.b007: Hesk goes to his knees, pulls off a glove, and lays both hands flat on the snow and the rock beneath it.
beats.ch06.s02.b008: One. A pause. One. That is not ours. Too fast. Too eager.
beats.ch06.s02.b009: Iron on iron. Down in the icefall.
beats.ch06.s02.b010: Nobody has any business down there.
beats.ch06.s02.b012: She strikes once more, and the answer comes back up through the ice inside a count of ten. Slow, the way cold carries a thing. And human.
beats.ch06.s03.b002: They are below. They hear us. We keep ringing.
beats.ch06.s03.b003: She stops at Hesk, and puts her face close to his so he can read her mouth.
beats.ch06.s03.b004: Steady. Slow it down. Do not let them run to us.
beats.ch06.s03.b005: They are coming to a sound in a whiteout. A man runs, he comes over a cornice, and then we are five bells short.
beats.ch06.s03.b006: That is exactly it. Ring slow. Four strikes, then rest. Let them walk to us one step at a time.
beats.ch06.s03.b007: He nods, and the nod has no argument in it at all, only the readiness of a man handed a thing to do.
beats.ch06.s03.b008: Four and a rest. I have got it. Go and be warm.
beats.ch06.s04.b002: Ilse puts the bar into Priya's hands and makes her take the rhythm. She sets Teodor where they can keep each other's warmth. She sets Hesk at the rope end.
beats.ch06.s04.b003: Now we work. That is the whole of the work. Four cold people busy enough not to lie down.
beats.ch06.s04.b004: One, two, three, four. Rest. One, two, three, four.
beats.ch06.s04.b005: You are a beat ahead of the mountain.
beats.ch06.s04.b007: Then ring slow. Cold is a reason, not an excuse.
beats.ch06.s04.b008: Ilse walks the circle a third time. The answer comes through the rock, not Priya's, then nearer, and she lets the counting go and counts only answers.
beats.ch06.s04.b009: The strokes come up the ridge one step at a time now, careful. A man who trusts his footing because he can feel it and cannot see it. The ringing stops. The feet come on.
beats.ch06.s04.b010: A shape walks out of the white into the small clear air around the slab. Ilse is on her feet before she has decided to be.
beats.ch06.s05.b002: He stands still and looks at the four of them and at the bell. Then he makes the sign Ilse taught him. I have been listening and at last I am here.
beats.ch06.s05.b005: Your head. It was full of loud water at the col.
beats.ch06.s05.b006: Dawa is below at the terrace with the line. Two more behind me from the rescue party, with the doctor. Slow.
beats.ch06.s05.b007: I lay down at the col and the ground went small and tight under me. I said to Dawa, the mountain is ringing like struck iron. So I got up and I came.
beats.ch06.s05.b008: The ringing is better than the lying down.
beats.ch06.s05.b009: Yes. Come. We go before the wind comes round again.
beats.ch06.s06.b002: The doctor takes one look at the ankle and speaks to Nima, and Teodor sits down at once and lets himself be laced and strapped, and does not argue.
beats.ch06.s06.b003: Teodor arguing was the mountain. Teodor sitting still is the road home.
beats.ch06.s06.b004: The strap stays on and he rides. No weight on it. Not one step.
beats.ch06.s06.b005: I have walked a good deal further on a worse foot.
beats.ch06.s06.b007: They strap him and lift him and set him on the litter, and Ilse sees the case strapped on her own back, because she is not going to hand it to anyone on a face where a man could go over.
beats.ch06.s07.b002: Nima goes first with a probe and a long step and a short one, tapping ahead like a blind man in his own house. Ilse goes second with her feet reading the ice through her soles.
beats.ch06.s07.b003: The hollows are lying. Nobody trusts a flat white place tonight.
beats.ch06.s07.b004: Then we step where I step and we do not step pretty.
beats.ch06.s07.b005: They bring the party down the way they brought them up. By feeling.

beats.ch06.s08.b004: The new one. East, under the wall.
beats.ch06.s08.b006: The sliding is done. I felt it coming down. It went quiet.
beats.ch06.s08.b007: Ilse lays her palm flat and holds it there. Quiet, and the quiet has the set of a thing that has finished moving.

beats.ch06.s09.b002: The rescue men take the points. Nima finds the way. The blocks are slotted and loose and a man's boot can go to the ankle between them.
beats.ch06.s09.b003: Here. Then left. Then the long step and do not look down.
beats.ch06.s09.b004: Priya. Snug the line. The litter goes where I go.
beats.ch06.s09.b005: The litter goes where you go.

beats.ch06.s10.b002: Ilse comes down the step and puts her hand under Priya's arm.
beats.ch06.s10.b003: Up. We are not stopping on the terrace.
beats.ch06.s10.b005: The crying has come on her all at once. It has the shape of a thing held under and come up. The tears are freezing as they come.
beats.ch06.s10.b006: I have to say it before we get down. Before base camp. Before any of them.
beats.ch06.s10.b007: You told me on the mountain.
