beats.ch06.s10.b009: I financed the whole of it so I could come up here and make my great-great-grandfather the hero of it.
beats.ch06.s10.b011: I would have done it. If it had not been for the boy with his glove. Tell me what the record has to call it.
beats.ch06.s10.b012: Ilse crouches down on the ice so that her face is level with Priya's. Her feet on the terrace tell her nothing is moving. Her hand on the case tells her it is steady and cold.
beats.ch06.s10.b013: The record calls it what you just did. You tried to burn a page and then you read it out loud to four people. You meant to bury the truth and then you carried it down a whiteout.
beats.ch06.s10.b015: It is a true one. There is a man in your family who rang a bell all night and could not hear it answered. There is a man in your family who wanted to take his page out of the book and did not.
beats.ch06.s10.b016: The book goes to the archive entire. I will see it published whole, and I will write the preface, and I will not be kind. Do you understand me? It will not be kind and it will be told.
beats.ch06.s10.b017: Then I will be the one to tell it.
beats.ch06.s10.b018: Hesk comes down the step with the bar in his fist. He has heard none of it and guessed most of it. He sets his hand flat on the block beside her.
beats.ch06.s10.b019: The case goes with her and nobody touches it. That is my part. The story is not mine.
beats.ch06.s10.b020: Get up, Priya. You will have years afterwards to be ashamed in. Do not do it on a terrace.
beats.ch06.s10.b021: Priya wipes her face with her mitten and makes a small business of it, and then stands straight.
beats.ch06.s11.b002: At the last terrace the wind is gone and the night is clear above. The bell comes down onto hard snow and stands.
beats.ch06.s11.b004: Then we ring once more and we let them know we are here and coming down.
beats.ch06.s11.b005: Ilse sets her feet flat on the snow, and the tone comes up through the ice into her boot soles and up the bones of her legs, a clean round note that goes out into the dark.
beats.ch06.s11.b006: She waits. The answer comes up through the ice, three beats and a pause and three beats, faint and steady, from the tents below.
beats.ch06.s11.b007: Four beats. Slow. Let them know.
beats.ch06.s11.b008: Hesk takes the bar and rings it. Ilse stands with her palm on the bronze and lets it go, and the whole mountain carries it down.
beats.ch06.s11.b009: They heard it all night. The whole line below. We were not ringing for nothing.
beats.ch06.s11.b010: There is no such thing as ringing for nothing. Come on. We have a road and it is downhill, and I intend to walk all of it.
beats.ch07.s01.b002: Ilse walks one slow circle of the camp. Her boots find snow and nothing else. No tremor, no creep.
beats.ch07.s01.b003: The ground has stopped moving. Best reading of the week.
beats.ch07.s01.b004: Water is hot. Drink it before it freezes again. That is my medical advice.
beats.ch07.s01.b005: I have decided to be cheerful. I want everyone to note how well it is going. For an ankle sprain on a high-altitude expedition, immediate care often involves careful management of the injury alongside altitude considerations.
beats.ch07.s01.b006: Note taken. How is the foot?
beats.ch07.s01.b007: The foot is not invited to this conversation.
beats.ch07.s01.b009: The far wall has come out of the cloud, black and clean, and the whole icefall with it, a wreck of frozen blocks glittering in the low sun.
beats.ch07.s01.b010: The line is set. All the way to the second terrace.
beats.ch07.s02.b002: Ilse walks with one hand on the line and her feet still awake. Strange to have the mountain outside her again, plain as a field, when she carried it all night inside her hands.
beats.ch07.s02.b003: Sorry. I keep looking at it. I did not expect to see any of it again.
beats.ch07.s02.b004: Look now. You may not pass this way again.
beats.ch07.s02.b005: I am crying in a tired way. I know. The danger is over and nobody has told my body.
beats.ch07.s02.b006: Nobody has told mine either. My shoulders are filing a complaint.
beats.ch07.s03.b002: Swelling. Bruise the colour of a storm. A small crack maybe in a bone. Not broken.
beats.ch07.s03.b003: He does not walk on it again today.
beats.ch07.s03.b004: I have walked on it all night.
beats.ch07.s03.b005: Then you have done enough walking on it for one man. The strap stays on. He rides.
beats.ch07.s03.b006: I will not argue with the litter.
beats.ch07.s03.b007: Then it hurts more than he will say.
beats.ch07.s03.b008: Teodor settles back, closes his eyes, and lifts one hand in the two-fingered wave that means he is all right and she is not to fuss. Ilse lays her palm on his shoulder and feels the shake in him under the coat.
beats.ch07.s04.b002: They stand at the top with the wall hanging over them in great soft ledges, and nobody speaks.
beats.ch07.s04.b003: East. Under the wall. That is how I came up.
beats.ch07.s04.b004: One at a time. The bell on the litter. The litter on the fixed line.
beats.ch07.s04.b005: Nobody walks beside the bell. That is the rule today. The party moves carefully across the ice, following established ropes and anchors to navigate around any large blocks of ice in the rubble field.
beats.ch07.s05.b002: Ilse stands at the corner and feels the litter come to her through her soles as much as through the ropes. Fifteen kilos of bronze, gone into the mountain a hundred and twelve years ago, coming down now by the hands of people who do not own it.
beats.ch07.s05.b004: The ice answers and holds. Hesk takes the next length and does not speak and does not take his eyes off the cradle.
beats.ch07.s05.b005: Priya comes down the fixed line behind it and says nothing for the whole of the fall. At the bottom she sets the case on clean snow and looks back up at the ruin they have come through.
beats.ch07.s05.b006: I want to do it properly.
beats.ch07.s05.b008: There is a man in the valley who has been sending me letters about the bell for a year. I have answered none of them. He has my name and my silence and his own newspaper.
beats.ch07.s05.b009: The archive first, before the paper. I want to stand in the east hall and hand the book over with my own name on the wrong end of it. Not the way I meant to. The proper way.
beats.ch07.s05.b010: The paper will not be kind.
beats.ch07.s05.b011: I have had enough of kind. Kind is what my mother gave me instead of the truth.
beats.ch07.s06.b002: Ilse sits down without first feeling the ground through her hands. That is the newest thing of the whole week.
beats.ch07.s06.b003: I am still noting the cheerfulness. It is going badly.
beats.ch07.s06.b004: You are grey to the chin.
beats.ch07.s06.b006: Hesk gets up. He comes over, puts a folded paper into her hand, and stands there. It is the pay slip, signed across the back.
beats.ch07.s06.b007: The bet. It is yours. Put it in the school.
beats.ch07.s06.b009: It is a start. And I am going to be the first one through the door.
beats.ch07.s06.b010: You will teach me the one thing I still cannot do. I will be some trouble.
beats.ch07.s06.b012: She puts the paper in her pocket. Hesk goes back to the wall and sits down, and that is the whole of the apology, made with his hands this time.
beats.ch07.s07.b002: Teodor is carried into the mess tent and put on a stretcher. The doctor comes and finds Ilse in the sun before she has finished her tea.
beats.ch07.s07.b003: The foot will heal. Off it weeks, on it by winter.
beats.ch07.s07.b004: Teodor is not lucky. Teodor is careful, and he was carrying a bell.
beats.ch07.s07.b005: The sponsor's man arrives at a walk that wants to be a run. He stands over the bell with his mouth open. The cook comes out, puts his palm on the bronze, and keeps it there.
beats.ch07.s07.b006: This is it. This is the bell from the cave. The whole story. How did you get it down?
beats.ch07.s07.b008: Miss Rask. The office told me. About your family. About the guide. It came up from the valley before I did. I have not known what to do with it.
beats.ch07.s07.b009: Write it. The whole of it. The cook rang the bell and the guide lay under a rock and the record gave the guide the credit.
beats.ch07.s07.b010: I am his great-great-granddaughter. I came up here to burn a page and I did not. Say that too.
beats.ch07.s07.b011: The slip is creased and grey at the edges, and the signature is large and careful, as though he had practised it.
beats.ch07.s07.b012: There is a burnt place on the first page the size of a man's glove. Beside it is a note in my own hand that says how it came there. Show it to your newspaper man. Nobody has to be flattered and nobody has to be spared.
beats.ch07.s07.b013: The sponsor's man makes a small sound in his throat and turns his clipboard over as if he has forgotten what it is for. He does not write anything down.
beats.ch07.s08.b002: Ilse walks the camp and feels it under her feet. The moraine is solid. Her feet tell her nothing at all, and nothing at all is the sweetest reading of the week.
beats.ch07.s08.b003: She counts them, as she counted them going up when the counting was a thing she would not do out loud. Nima and Dawa at the stove, both whole. Teodor asleep with his foot up. Priya reading the burnt page aloud to nobody, getting it right.
beats.ch07.s08.b004: Hesk stands at the bell looking at it the way a man looks at a thing that has beaten him and that he has come to love.
beats.ch07.s08.b005: Eleven walked up. Eleven are on the shelf. The mountain has taken a week, an ankle, and a good deal of our pride.
beats.ch07.s09.b002: From the valley. The forecast desk.
beats.ch07.s09.b003: Storm in from the west. They say four days. They say hold the camp. But the valley is already white, and the barometer dropped faster than the model.
beats.ch07.s09.b004: There is a man in the city who has looked at the same figures. He says two days, and he is usually right. The road out is under snow as far as the bridge.
beats.ch07.s09.b005: Ilse goes past him to the edge of the shelf and stands on the old rock and takes her boots' reading.
beats.ch07.s09.b006: The glacier is not quiet. There is a pressure under the nothing. A long low shifting. The ground gone very slightly heavy, the way a slope feels a moment before it decides.
beats.ch07.s09.b007: She comes back to the group.
beats.ch07.s09.b008: Two days. The valley is right and the desk has been wrong about the same weather all week.
beats.ch07.s09.b009: We go for the bridge at first light. The bell, the book, the boy with the bad foot. If the bridge is gone, we go over the moraine the hard way and we go on foot.
beats.ch07.s09.b010: On foot, with a litter, in a storm?
beats.ch07.s09.b011: On foot with a litter, or we are still on this mountain when it shuts.
beats.ch07.s09.b012: She goes to the mess tent door. Teodor is awake on the stretcher and does not ask what has happened, because he can read her as well as she reads ground.
beats.ch07.s09.b015: I can be carried. It is a different skill, and I have been practising it all morning.
beats.ch07.s10.b002: Hesk is already looking at the yellow edge of the sky. She does not have to tell him anything.
beats.ch07.s10.b003: The stakes go with us. The tent, the rope, the stove, the shovel. I will see to it tonight.
beats.ch07.s10.b004: Tell me what you want me to feel for, on the road, in the dark. You taught me the floor and the anchor. Teach me the weather.
beats.ch07.s10.b005: Ilse turns his burned palm upward and lays her own over it.
beats.ch07.s10.b006: The wind comes from the west before the snow. Put your hand on the ground and feel the change in it. When the ice goes from quiet to listening, come and tell me.
beats.ch07.s10.b007: Ring the bell if the radio dies. You know the four now.
beats.ch07.s10.b009: He closes his fingers over hers and lets go. Ilse walks out to the edge of the shelf once more and stands with her back to the camp and the whole white length of the glacier going down toward the valley.
beats.ch07.s10.b010: The glass is falling. The mountain is not letting us go after all.
beats.ch08.s01.b002: Ilse presses her palm to the stone. The machines in the belly of the building turn, and the turning comes up through her soles, a fine steady hum. Like standing on the skin of a sleeping animal.
beats.ch08.s01.b003: A reporter leans in with a recorder. He asks, slowly and loudly, whether she needs help up the steps.
beats.ch08.s01.b004: I can feel the building. I can hear your question. Neither of those is the trouble.
beats.ch08.s01.b005: Priya goes up ahead of them with the case. The reporters make a lane, the way a river makes a lane around a stone.
beats.ch08.s01.b006: There are more of them than there were of us on the whole mountain.
beats.ch08.s02.b002: The floorboards lean. A hundred people, all leaning the same way. A boat leans like that when everyone aboard has gone to one rail.
beats.ch08.s02.b003: Miss Marchetti. We have kept you a seat at the front. The committee will hear us after.
beats.ch08.s02.b004: Then let us give them something to hear.
beats.ch08.s03.b002: For a hundred and twelve years, this painting has told you that a guide named Karel Vasek rang the bell in the storm of the eleventh of September, nineteen hundred and eight.
beats.ch08.s03.b003: I am Anders Weiss's great-great-granddaughter, and I am here to tell you that the painting is wrong.
beats.ch08.s03.b004: Nobody moves. The hall has the pressure of held breath.
beats.ch08.s03.b005: The man who rang the bell was the cook. The cook was deaf. He rang in four strikes and a pause, from midnight until dawn, and six men lived. The guide lay unconscious under a rock and did not wake until it was over.
beats.ch08.s03.b006: This is his ledger. He wrote down every hour of that night, and every name, and how he rang.
beats.ch08.s03.b007: She lifts the logbook and the framed page together so the lights catch them.
beats.ch08.s03.b008: The first page was burned by me. In the ice cave, on the mountain, with the flame I carried up there for the purpose. I meant to finish the job and burn the rest. Hesk Vandry crushed it out with his glove, and the hole is the size of that glove, and both of those things are the record now.
beats.ch08.s03.b009: I intended to come home with a book that agreed with me. I intended to bury him again. I want that written down with the rest of it.
beats.ch08.s03.b010: She sets the logbook down and puts her hand flat on the glass.
beats.ch08.s03.b011: The shame is not that my great-great-grandfather was a cook. The shame is that this building hung his picture and called him a coward and did not look for the truth for a hundred and twelve years. I ask the archive to change the wall.
beats.ch08.s03.b012: Nobody claps. The holding goes on so long Ilse feels it as pressure in the boards. Then a woman in the front row stands, and another, and the clapping comes unevenly, like hail.
beats.ch08.s03.b013: Near the back a heavyset man in a work coat is on his feet, shouting that a cook cannot have rung a bell he could not hear. Ilse feels his stamping through the floor the way she felt the slab move on the hanging slope.
beats.ch08.s03.b014: Anger through the floor, I trust. The rest I do not.
beats.ch08.s03.b015: The rest is a wet room and a warm coat. Let it run.
beats.ch08.s04.b002: The young clerk lays a letter on the table and smooths it flat with two fingers, as though it might otherwise get away.
beats.ch08.s04.b003: Delivered a week ago. A nephew of a nephew of Karel Vasek writes that the bell was Vasek's property, carried up by Vasek's men, and that we hold it without title. He asks us to determine ownership before the bell is exhibited.
beats.ch08.s04.b004: There is a second letter from the newspaper. Their man wants the claim heard in public, and a statement.
beats.ch08.s04.b005: That is what we shall write down. Whose bell is it?
beats.ch08.s04.b006: Vasek's men carried it up. A cook rang it. A nephew of a nephew is welcome to the account and not welcome to the bell.
beats.ch08.s04.b007: The five look at one another. The young clerk lifts his pen and does not write with it. Ilse feels the hesitation go round the table through the wood, a rope going soft when everyone on it has stopped pulling.
beats.ch08.s04.b008: Then say this, and write it exactly. The archive has examined the claim. The bell was raised by an expedition and given to the people of this city, and any man who believes he owns it may put his belief before a court, at his own cost, and the archive will meet him there.
beats.ch08.s04.b009: That is the statement. Print it under whatever headline you like. And tell your man at the back of the hall that we have heard him shout.
beats.ch08.s04.b010: A bell rung by a deaf man is a bell rung by a man who could feel it and not hear it. That is the whole of what this building has failed to understand for a hundred and twelve years.
beats.ch08.s04.b011: I have that. I have all of it.
beats.ch08.s04.b012: The bell came off the mountain in the hands of a deaf guide, a cook's great-great-granddaughter, and a boy who bet against them both. It can sit here while the lawyers enjoy themselves. It is not going far.
beats.ch08.s04.b013: Miss Marchetti. You led the expedition. You are deaf. And the boy who bet against you is enrolling in this school I keep hearing about.
beats.ch08.s04.b014: He is the first one through the door. He says he will say he was wrong every year until they are sick of him.
beats.ch08.s04.b015: The thin archivist holds Ilse a while over her glasses. Then she turns to the table and sets her hand flat on the wet wood.
beats.ch08.s04.b016: Then I move we put the cook's name on the wall before the lawyers put the bell in a cupboard. This archive has told a wrong story for a hundred and twelve years, and I shall enjoy writing the correction.
beats.ch08.s04.b017: And I should like to hear about the school. Education is our business here. If we have been telling children the wrong story, we should be the ones to tell them the right one, and tell them who carried it down.
beats.ch08.s04.b018: That is how it begins. A thin old woman, a sentence, a wet window. Before the committee rises, it has become a grant.
beats.ch08.s05.b002: Hesk comes in from the street with his coat dripping and stands at the plinth. The hall goes quiet in a soft way, the way a room goes quiet for a boy who is about to do something difficult.
beats.ch08.s05.b003: I said I would say this at the school. Then I thought, the trouble with a quiet apology is that the ones who need to hear it are usually not in the room.
beats.ch08.s05.b004: I bet a week's pay that a deaf guide would call a crevasse that was not there. I did it on the first morning, in front of the whole expedition.
beats.ch08.s05.b005: I said it because I did not want to believe someone could feel the mountain in a way I never would, and because a bet was easier than being frightened.
beats.ch08.s05.b006: He looks at Ilse across the hall. She does not move, and she does not help him.
beats.ch08.s05.b007: She called the real crevasse on the glacier. The serac in the icefall. The slab on the hanging slope. The hollow under the new snow that took Teodor Brann's ankle. The east face loose, when I was all for going down it with four men and a bell.
beats.ch08.s05.b008: I was wrong every time. I told her so on the mountain, and I am telling the city so in this building, so it will go in the record with the rest.
beats.ch08.s05.b009: The slip is creased and grey at the edges. The signature is large and careful, as though he practised it.
beats.ch08.s05.b010: My week's pay. It is the first money in the school. I am the first pupil, and I will say this every year on the first day until they are tired of me.
beats.ch08.s05.b011: A woman near the front says something to her neighbour. The neighbour shakes her head and smiles at the boy by the bell with his wet coat and his folded paper.
beats.ch08.s05.b012: He paid it in money at the bottom, as he said he would.
beats.ch08.s05.b013: He paid it twice. The mountain took the first one.
beats.ch08.s06.b002: Four pupils. That is all the money there is. One of them is Hesk, two were told all their lives that a deaf guide was a kindness and not a trade, and one came because his parents think he is here to learn rope work.
beats.ch08.s06.b003: I am not teaching you this because I am fit. I am teaching you this because I am not.
beats.ch08.s06.b004: If a man cannot climb for a season, he can still teach what he knows. A school that only teaches when the teacher is fit is a school with no teachers in it half the year.
beats.ch08.s06.b005: He puts Hesk on a bight of rope and makes him tie it until his fingers know it better than his brain. He does not talk while he ties.
beats.ch08.s06.b006: The first way was a guess. I do not teach guesses. Tie it again.
beats.ch08.s06.b007: Master Brann. Is it true you came down the mountain carried?
beats.ch08.s06.b008: It is true. And every man on that ridge carried something, and the heaviest thing was a bell. Now tie it.
beats.ch08.s06.b009: Put the rope down. Coats on. We are going up the screes before the light.
beats.ch08.s07.b002: Ilse walks the line and sets a hand on each shoulder. Then she stands back.
beats.ch08.s07.b003: Boots on the ground. Eyes shut. Do not listen.
beats.ch08.s07.b005: You are not listening. You are feeling. The stones tell you how they lie. Put the whole of your foot down and wait.
beats.ch08.s07.b006: They stand in the cold for an hour. Nobody feels anything, and nobody admits it. The wind moves over the scree and the loose stones chatter somewhere below.
beats.ch08.s07.b007: The wind is coming from the east. The stones are ringing on that side. I can feel them ring.
beats.ch08.s07.b008: Good. That is the wind on the stones. Now feel the difference when it is a man.
beats.ch08.s07.b009: She walks down the slope behind them, and they feel her come before they turn round. The boy of sixteen laughs out loud, once, and puts his hand over his mouth.
beats.ch08.s07.b010: A boy in a snow cave with his palm on the ice, asking whether the mountain was always talking. It is always talking. The trick is to be still enough to hear.
beats.ch08.s08.b002: Three places a year. Tuition, bed and board, boots and a coat. Two from the valley and one from anywhere.
beats.ch08.s08.b003: It is not enough to be rich and it is too much to be nothing, and the interest on my flat will pay for it if I am careful and do not eat in restaurants.
beats.ch08.s08.b004: I want it called the Weiss Scholarship. If the archive wishes to put my name to the money, it may, in small letters, at the bottom, where the lawyers find it and the visitors do not.
beats.ch08.s08.b005: Your name will not be small. It is in the preface. I wrote it.
beats.ch08.s08.b006: I have read the draft. You called me a coward and a fool, and then you said I brought the book down off the mountain and gave it to the men who would hate me for it.
beats.ch08.s08.b007: A woman who does that has paid for the bell twice, once in money and once in shame. I have not been called a fool in print before. It is a great deal better than being pitied.
beats.ch08.s08.b008: Then the big letters are his, and the small letters are yours, and mine are at the bottom saying I am deaf and led by touch. That is the whole of the order.
beats.ch08.s08.b009: And my name is on nothing at all, which suits me. I have a stool and a stick and a class of guesses to correct.
beats.ch08.s09.b002: The card says: In preparation — Portrait of Anders Weiss, Cook, 1908. Beneath it a smaller card says the painting previously on this wall may be studied in the east annexe, under glass, with a label containing the word wrong eleven times.
beats.ch08.s09.b003: I counted them. It is the finest thing this building has ever done.
beats.ch08.s09.b004: I wrote it. I did not write one of the elevens by accident.
beats.ch08.s09.b005: I have climbed with this woman nineteen years and she never once told me what she was going to do before she did it. Now she has a preface that says the whole of it in plain words.
beats.ch08.s09.b006: I did not recognise her in it. She is much better company in the preface than she is at four in the morning on a snow slope.
beats.ch08.s09.b007: The thin archivist laughs until she has to take her glasses off. Priya does not cry and is not grey. She looks at the word wrong on the card as though she has walked there from very far away.
beats.ch08.s09.b010: We are a library. If a bell cannot be rung in a library, where may it be rung?
beats.ch08.s09.b011: Ilse walks to the middle of the hall and sets her palm to the floor. The building is quiet. The city hums through the stones, indifferent to the whole business of the hall.
beats.ch08.s09.b012: She feels the bell on its plinth, a small dense weight above the boards, and the people standing round her, and the winter cold coming in at the open door.
beats.ch08.s09.b014: Hesk swings the bar once and the bell speaks. Ilse does not hear it. She feels it come through the plinth and the old boards and up into her boots, a great round tone rolling out into the stone.
beats.ch08.s09.b015: It rang in a cave in an ice cliff in nineteen hundred and eight and brought six men home. It rang on the Ridge of Echoes in a whiteout and brought four.
beats.ch08.s09.b016: It rings now among wet streets and people going home to supper, and one of the people standing in it is a deaf woman from the valley with the whole of the bell in her bones.
beats.ch08.s09.b017: Somebody somewhere is feeling this and does not yet know what it is.
beats.ch08.s09.b019: He rings it again. The tone goes through her and through the hall and out, and she thinks of a school above a bakery and a boy who bet against her and was the first through its door.
beats.ch08.s09.b020: Again. One more, and then we will go and eat.
beats.ch08.s09.b021: The third note rolls out under the door and down the steps into the winter air. Hesk sets the bar down. Priya puts her hand on the glass case. Nobody in the hall says anything at all.
